solutions.latex:

Then compound this for 2 years at $1.25\%$ per annum.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 8213.20\times(1.0125)^2 \\ &\approx \$8419.81 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the balance after 10 years is } \$8419.81$$

parts.latex: Julia invests \$250 per month in an annuity which pays 5.4% p.a. compounding monthly. What will be the value of the annuity after 5 years?

Carrington finds that he can only get an interest rate of 3.6% p.a. compounding annually.

If he wants to achieve the same total amount as Julia after the same period, what amount should he invest each month?

solutions.latex:
Monthly payments at $5.4\%$ p.a. compounding monthly, so the rate per period is
$$\dfrac{5.4\%}{12} = 0.45\%$$
The number of periods is $5\times 12 = 60$.

From the table, the interest factor for $0.45\%$ and $60$ periods is $68.7047$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{FV} &= 250 \times 68.7047 \\ &= \$17\,176.18 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the annuity is worth } \$17\,176.18 \text{ (to the nearest cent)}$$
criteria: Identifies the factor $68.7047$ (rate $0.45\%$, $60$ periods), or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Carrington must reach the same amount, $\$17\,176.18$ (using $\$17\,176.175$ unrounded), after the same $60$ months.

The question says compounding annually, but the table (and the answer key) work per month, so this takes $0.30\%$ per month:
$$\dfrac{3.6\%}{12} = 0.30\%$$
From the table, the factor for $0.30\%$ and $60$ periods is $65.6316$.

Let the monthly investment be $M$. Then
$$\begin{aligned} M \times 65.6316 &= 17\,176.175 \\ M &= \dfrac{17\,176.175}{65.6316} \\ &\approx 261.71 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Carrington should invest } \$261.71 \text{ each month}$$
criteria: Uses the factor $65.6316$ ($0.30\%$, $60$ periods) in an equation for the monthly amount, or equivalent merit

Kim deposits \$4200 each year for 3 years. The annuity earns $4\%$ per annum, compounded annually.

What is the lump sum, to the nearest dollar, that Kim could have deposited when she opened the account, in order to achieve the same result over 3 years at $4\%$ per annum, compounded annually?

solutions.latex:
Final value of Kim's annuity $=4200\times 3.122$.

For a lump sum $P$ to achieve the same result:
$$\begin{aligned}4200\times 3.122&=P\times(1.04)^3\\P&=\dfrac{4200\times 3.122}{(1.04)^3}\\&=\$11\,656.88\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore P\approx\$11\,657 \text{ (to the nearest dollar)}$$
Hence option B is correct.

Sakein is saving for a holiday to Europe in twelve months time. She needs at least \$6000 for the trip.

She has decided to put \$500 each month into a special bank account that pays interest that compounds monthly.

parts.latex: What is the monthly interest rate?
If she chose to invest one lump sum at the start of the twelve months, instead of making the monthly deposits of \$500, how much would she have had to invest to get the same final amount?

solutions.latex:
The interest in the first month is $\$2.50$ on a balance of $\$500$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Monthly rate} &= \dfrac{2.50}{500} \\ &= 0.5\% \text{ per month} \end{aligned}$$

$A$ and $B$ are the balance at the end of the month and the start of the next month.
$$\begin{aligned} A = B &= 5114.01 + 25.57 + 500 \\ &= \$5639.58 \end{aligned}$$
$C$ is the interest on $B$ at $0.5\%$.
$$\begin{aligned} C &= 0.005 \times 5639.58 \\ &= \$28.20 \end{aligned}$$
$D$ is the monthly deposit.
$$D = \$500.00$$
criteria: Calculates the interest, or equivalent merit
Finds the balance at the end of the month and the start of the following month, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the compound interest formula, the lump sum $PV$ grows to the final amount over 12 months at $0.5\%$ per month.
$$6167.78 = PV \times 1.005^{12}$$
$$\begin{aligned} PV &= 6167.78 \div 1.005^{12} \\ &= \$5809.46 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Applies compound interest formula, or equivalent merit
